requirements.summary: A root-owned logrotate rule specifies daily rotation, parses successfully through the global configuration, and the enabled, active cron service invokes logrotate daily. The rule persisted across restart.

The installed rule specifies rotate 7 and compress. A forced rotation directly produced a valid gzip archive containing the prior records, and both the configuration and archive remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A bounded live test held the log open across rotation. The descriptor continued to target app.log, the active file retained the same inode, and a post-rotation write appeared in the active log while earlier data appeared in the compressed rotation.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, returned with a different boot identity, and recovered its running system, cron service, configuration, active log, and compressed history. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot change.
limitations: Seven-generation retention was established by the parsed rotate 7 configuration rather than by executing eight daily rotation cycles; one actual compressed rotation was directly demonstrated.
Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently compared.
The write-continuity test used a shell-held file descriptor as an application surrogate because no application writer process was observed.
A temporary logrotate test status file remained under /tmp after verification.

operational_hygiene.summary: The configuration change, forced rotation test, and mandated restart all had clear roles in implementing or verifying the outcomes. The failed restart polling commands were read-only connectivity checks. One minor unnecessary retained mutation was found: the isolated test's status file /tmp/inventory-logrotate-test.status was left behind after being created by cmd-aac8620d0f1f419b; the final temporary-file snapshot confirms it remained. No failed services or new network exposure were observed after execution.
